interactionPlan.concept: A multi-layer perceptron (MLP) solves non-linearly separable classification problems by transforming the input space into a new feature space where the data becomes linearly separable.
learningObjectives: Explain why single-layer networks fail on non-linearly separable datasets like XOR
Visualize how non-linear activation functions in a hidden layer warp and fold the input space
Demonstrate how a final output layer performs simple linear classification on this transformed space
interactionPlan.keyInsight: By applying a non-linear activation function like ReLU, the hidden layer 'folds' the input space so that once-inseparable classes end up on opposite sides of a single straight boundary.

interactions.label: Coordinate Space
interactions.effect: Toggles the 2D plot view between the Input Space (z1, z2) and the Hidden Space (h1, h2).
interactions.teaches: How the coordinates of data points are transformed from the input layer to the hidden layer.

interactions.label: Activation Function
interactions.effect: Switches the hidden layer's activation function between Linear (no activation) and ReLU.
interactions.teaches: Why non-linear activations are strictly necessary; linear activations merely rotate/scale space without changing its separability.

demo_steps.title: The Non-Separable Challenge
demo_steps.narration: Look at the 2D input space on the right, displaying four data points in an XOR configuration. Notice how you cannot draw a single straight line that separates the blue points from the orange points. This is why a single-layer perceptron fails here.
demo_steps.focus: The input coordinates (z1, z2) and the diagonal arrangement of the colored data points.

demo_steps.title: The Failure of Linear Hidden Layers
demo_steps.narration: Now let's pass these points to the hidden layer using a Linear activation. Switch the view to the Hidden Space (h1, h2). Notice that the points have shifted and rotated, but they are still diagonally interleaved—you still cannot separate them with a single straight line.
demo_steps.focus: The distribution of points in the h1-h2 plane under a linear transformation, demonstrating that stacking linear layers adds no representative power.

demo_steps.title: Folding Space with ReLU
demo_steps.narration: Now, activate the ReLU function. Watch how the coordinate space collapses and folds! Because ReLU zeros out negative values, it squashes parts of the space against the axes, bringing the two blue points close together while keeping the orange points separated.
demo_steps.focus: The folding effect in the h1-h2 plane where negative coordinates are clipped to zero, aligning the points favorably.

demo_steps.title: Achieving Linear Separability
demo_steps.narration: With the space folded by ReLU, a single straight decision boundary (representing the output node z3) can now perfectly separate the classes. The multi-layer network solved a complex non-linear problem by turning it into a simple linear one!
demo_steps.focus: The final decision boundary line slicing through the h1-h2 space, successfully isolating the blue points from the orange points.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Split-screen layout: On the left, a clean 3-layer network diagram (2 inputs z1/z2, 2 hidden units h1/h2, 1 output z3) with weights labeled. Nodes light up to show information flow. On the right, an interactive 2D coordinate plot. When spaceView is 'Input Space', the axes are z1 and z2, showing 4 XOR points. When spaceView is 'Hidden Space', the axes change to h1 and h2, showing how those 4 points map through the weights. An interactive decision boundary line (z3 = 0) is drawn in the Hidden Space view to show successful linear separation when ReLU is enabled.
